root_cause: The Datepicker.hide() method incorrectly checks `this.active` (which doesn't exist on Datepicker) instead of `this.picker.active`, causing it to return early without hiding. Additionally, no blur event listener exists to close the datepicker when focus leaves the input via keyboard (Tab).
repair_strategy: Fix Datepicker.hide() to delegate to picker.hide() without the faulty guard, and add a blur listener on the input field that calls hide() for non-inline pickers.

edits.after:
const listeners = [
        [inputField, 'keydown', onKeydown.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'focus', onFocus.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'mousedown', onMousedown.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'click', onClickInput.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'paste', onPaste.bind(null, this)],
        [inputField, 'blur', () => { if (!this.inline) this.hide(); }],
        [document, 'mousedown', onMousedownDocument],
        [document, 'touchstart', onMousedownDocument],
        [window, 'resize', picker.place.bind(picker)]
      ];

expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can close the datepicker by moving focus away with Tab, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The datepicker now properly hides on blur for non-inline instances.
functional_risks: Blur fires on any focus loss (e.g., opening a popup), but guarded by !this.inline.
Inline pickers remain unaffected due to the inline check.
Duplicate hide calls are safe because Picker.hide() is idempotent.
verification_requirements: After typing a date and pressing Tab, the datepicker must close (.datepicker not visible).
Clicking on the datepicker or selecting a date via mouse/keyboard should still work and hide appropriately.
Inline datepickers should not be affected by the blur listener.
Focus should move to the next tabbable element (#instructions) as before.
